_note: Simulates a realistic 200-with-HTML-from-a-proxy response for the per-stop endpoint (final review, IMPORTANT 4) -- e.g. a captive portal or misconfigured reverse proxy answering with an HTML interstitial instead of the real API body, at HTTP 200 (so http_status-based fixtures like http-503.json don't exercise this). fetch_json's TWO-ARGUMENT json.decode(body, None) must return None on this body rather than raise; reverting fetch_json to resp.json() (single-argument, or the raw pixlet http.star .json() call) is FATAL on non-JSON bodies and crashes the render. No earlier fixture could express this: make_handler always json.dumps()'d its response body, so nothing could serve genuinely non-JSON bytes until stop_raw_body existed. With correct code, data == None makes both directions render the 'no trains' placeholder and the divider stays intact -- proven by mutating fetch_json back to resp.json() and confirming this fixture (only this fixture) starts crashing.
